'''Valentin Alfredovich Franke''' ({{langx|ru|Валенти́н Альфре́дович Фрáнке}}; 16 February 1926 – 31 January 2025) was a Soviet and Russian theoretical physicist and academic. A [[Doctor of Sciences]], he was professor of the High Energy & Elementary Particle at the Physics Department of [[Saint Petersburg State University]].

== Background and early career ==
V. A. Franke graduated from [[Igor Sikorsky Kyiv Polytechnic Institute|Kyiv Polytechnic Institute]] in 1949. After that he was [[Job by distribution|distributed]] to a power plant in [[Amur Oblast]], [[Russian Far East]]. In 1954 he externally graduated from [[Saint Petersburg State University|Leningrad State University]] and then worked in Institute of Labor Protection in Leningrad.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Valentin A. Franke|url=http://hep.phys.spbu.ru/science/franke_e.htm|access-date=14 March 2021|archive-date=21 February 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250221195937/http://hep.phys.spbu.ru/science/franke_e.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 1962 V. A. Franke joined the physical faculty of [[Leningrad State University|LSU]]. He obtained his [[Candidate of Sciences|PhD]] under the supervision of Yury Novozhilov in 1965 and was [[Doktor nauk|habilitated]] in 1984. He was a professor of High Energy & Elementary Particle Physics Department until his retirement in 2020. 

== Scientific and educational activity ==
Franke worked in the fields of [[Particle physics|elementary particle physics]], [[quantum mechanics]] and [[Gravity|theory of gravitation]]. He wrote more than 70 papers on these topics.

In 1976, Franke obtained the general form of the renowned [[Lindbladian|master equation]] for the evolution of [[density matrix]]. This equation was derived independently and simultaneously by V. A. Franke,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Franke|first=V. A.|date=1976|title=On the general form of the dynamical transformation of density matrices|url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF01051230|journal=Theoretical and Mathematical Physics|language=en|volume=27|issue=2|pages=406–413|doi=10.1007/BF01051230|s2cid=123168620 |issn=0040-5779|url-access=subscription}}</ref> [[Göran Lindblad (physicist)|G. Lindblad]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Lindblad|first=G.|date=1976|title=On the generators of quantum dynamical semigroups|url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF01608499|journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics|language=en|volume=48|issue=2|pages=119–130|doi=10.1007/BF01608499|s2cid=55220796 |issn=0010-3616|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and V. Gorini, [[Andrzej Kossakowski|A. Kossakowski]] and [[E. C. George Sudarshan|E. C. G. Sudarshan]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Gorini|first1=V.|last2=Kossakowski|first2=A.|last3=Sudarshan|first3=E. C. G.|date=1976|title=Completely positive dynamical semigroups of N‐level systems|journal=Journal of Mathematical Physics|volume=17|issue=5 |pages=821|doi=10.1063/1.522979}}</ref> (see <ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Chruściński|first1=Dariusz|last2=Pascazio|first2=Saverio|date=2017|title=A Brief History of the GKLS Equation|url=https://www.worldscientific.com/doi/abs/10.1142/S1230161217400017|journal=Open Systems & Information Dynamics|language=en|volume=24|issue=3|pages=1740001|doi=10.1142/S1230161217400017|issn=1230-1612|arxiv=1710.05993|s2cid=90357 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Andrianov|first1=A A|last2=Ioffe|first2=M V|last3=Novikov|first3=O O|date=18 October 2019|title=Supersymmetrization of the Franke–Gorini–Kossakowski–Lindblad–Sudarshan equation|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1751-8121/ab4338|journal=Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical|volume=52|issue=42|pages=425301|doi=10.1088/1751-8121/ab4338|issn=1751-8113|arxiv=1901.03848|s2cid=153312733 }}</ref>). FGKLS (Franke-Gorini-Kossakowski-Lindblad-Sudarshan) equation plays an important role in the description of open quantum systems and the quantum measurement theory. V. A. Franke himself considered this equation as a natural generalisation of standard quantum mechanics, whose validity has to be proven experimentally.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Franke|first=V. A.|date=2006|title=The foundations of quantum theory and its possible generalizations|journal=Proceedings of the 15th International V. A. Fock School for Advances of Physics 2005|editor-last=Novozhilov|editor-first=V.|publisher=SPbU Publ.|arxiv=2103.05374}}</ref>

From 1981, Franke and his colleagues have been working on the [[light front quantization]] of the [[Yang–Mills theory|Yang—Mills theory]]. This approach proves itself useful in non-perturbative description of [[quantum chromodynamics]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bakker|first1=B.L.G.|last2=Bassetto|first2=A.|last3=Brodsky|first3=S.J.|last4=Broniowski|first4=W.|last5=Dalley|first5=S.|last6=Frederico|first6=T.|last7=Głazek|first7=S.D.|last8=Hiller|first8=J.R.|last9=Ji|first9=C.-R.|last10=Karmanov|first10=V.|last11=Kulshreshtha|first11=D.|display-authors=3|date=2014|title=Light-front quantum chromodynamics|url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0920563214000930|journal=Nuclear Physics B - Proceedings Supplements|language=en|volume=251-252|pages=165–174|doi=10.1016/j.nuclphysbps.2014.05.004|arxiv=1309.6333|bibcode=2014NuPhS.251..165B |s2cid=117029089 }}</ref>

After the death of his long-time friend and colleague, [[Yuri Yappa]], V. A. Franke had completed and edited his unfinished monograph on the [[spinor]] theory.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Yappa|first=Yu. A.|title=An Introduction to Spinor Theory and Its Applications in Physics|publisher=SPb State University Publ.|year=2004|isbn=5-288-01951-7|editor-last=Franke|editor-first=V. A.|location=Saint Petersburg}}</ref>

== Death ==
Franke died on 31 January 2025, at the age of 98.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ушёл из жизни Валентин Альфредович Франке |url=https://hep.spbu.ru/index.php/ru/news |access-date=1 February 2025 |publisher=hep.spbu.ru |date=1 February 2025}}</ref>
